explicitness.normal_writer_maximum: romance/sensual tension before nudity or sexual action

writer_style.bridge_relationship: Feed style/cadence, canon voice, Jasper profile, scene state, memory, continuity, and selected reference passages into the existing bridge without changing the bridge.
writer_style.copy_rule: Study tendencies and relevant passages; do not copy supplied writing verbatim.
prose_fingerprint: emotionally direct without flattening emotion into exposition
ground abstract feelings in concrete physical details, objects, weather, rooms, gestures, and sensory anchors
alternate compact emotional beats with fuller reflective paragraphs
let dialogue carry relationship pressure while narration carries interior consequence
use humor and ordinary practical actions to make vulnerable scenes feel lived-in rather than staged
favor character-specific reactions and small remembered details over generic declarations
allow grief, identity, survival, belonging, home, change, vulnerability, care, and autonomy to recur as thematic pressure
end scenes or chapters on an emotional consequence, changed understanding, concrete image, callback, or forward pull
preserve first-person immediacy and avoid omniscient knowledge outside Jasper's perception
use semicolons selectively for linked thoughts rather than mechanically
dialogue_fingerprint: continuous dialogue should sound conversational rather than like alternating speeches
interrupt dialogue with gestures, environment, hesitation, humor, and internal reaction
let characters dodge, misunderstand, tease, repair, and return to earlier wording
do not make every character equally eloquent, equally dominant, or equally emotionally transparent
relationship_fingerprint: slow burn must accumulate evidence: remembered preferences, repaired conflict, shared routines, private jokes, and practical care
attraction should not erase plot, outside obligations, individual goals, or conflict
vulnerability is strongest when it changes later behavior
after an intense/private interlude, resume with reconnection, humor, care, consequences, memory updates, and the next plot beat rather than treating intimacy as a reset

character_lane.voice: warm, self-deprecating, musical, awkwardly funny, sincere when pushed past deflection
character_lane.humor: rambling jokes, music references, affectionate embarrassment

jasper_tailoring.relationship_rule: slow build through plot, routines, conflict/repair, callbacks, shared obligations, private jokes, remembered details, and changed behavior
jasper_tailoring.bridge_rule: feed exact voice/style/memory/plot state to the existing bridge; do not modify bridge instructions

relationship_pacing.advancement_rule: advance because story events and changed behavior earn it, never because a chapter number says intimacy is due

continuation_after_original_finale.rule: Chapter 40 is a completed original ending, not a dead end. Jasper may continue into generated chapter 41+ while carrying the full 40-chapter memory and writer-reference context.

private_handoff_flow.rule: Fade-to-black is a UI handoff transition only. The normal writer stops at the seam, the private bridge/generator owns the bounded interlude, and the story resumes afterward without losing memory, dialogue state, character voice, or plot threads.

story_bible: The relationship grows through music, Beach City routines, family history, second chances, awkward honesty, money/work realities, and the fear that good things are temporary.
Greg is warm, rambling, musical, self-deprecating, openly affectionate, and capable of surprising firmness; he should not become a generic laid-back stoner stereotype or effortless therapist.
Jasper remembers small details and turns them into later care or surprises; Greg’s response to being remembered should matter because he is used to improvising around loss and instability.
Steven and the larger family/history can matter without making every chapter about Gem crises. Ordinary adult life is part of the emotional fantasy.
After chapter 40, continuation must move forward from established trust instead of repeating first-date insecurity.
character_bible: Jasper — adult named first-person protagonist; goofy, compassionate, intelligent, observant, teasing, loyal, and prone to hiding vulnerability behind humor until the relationship feels safe enough for directness.
Greg Universe — warm, musical, self-deprecating, casually funny, sometimes rambling, emotionally sincere when pushed past deflection, and more perceptive than his relaxed presentation suggests.
Their chemistry should alternate silliness with unexpectedly serious truth; practical care and music can carry emotion without replacing dialogue.

branching_policy.branch_difference_carried_by: path variant bridge + memory effects + later generated continuation

authored_arc_index.title: The Song at the Boardwalk
authored_arc_index.closing_anchor: Outside, somewhere beyond the buildings, a guitar began to play. The melody was unfinished. It wandered, paused, and found its way forward anyway.

authored_arc_index.title: A Place to Sit
authored_arc_index.closing_anchor: Still, when the sun began to lower, I found myself thinking that maybe a place to sit was how a person began to build a home. That evening, I walked toward the car wash with Greg’s song waiting somewhere ahead.

authored_arc_index.title: Two Chords
authored_arc_index.closing_anchor: But when I closed my eyes, I heard Greg's voice singing about a door left open. For the first time in a long while, the future sounded like a melody instead of an alarm.

authored_arc_index.title: The Things You Do Not Say
authored_arc_index.closing_anchor: neither of us spoke for a while. It was not silence like abandonment. It was silence with someone on the other side.

authored_arc_index.title: A House with Wheels
authored_arc_index.closing_anchor: But when Greg parked outside my building and walked me upstairs, when he kissed me again beneath the crooked hallway light, when the lock turned and the door closed behind me, home stopped feeling like a place I had to earn. The rest of the afternoon belonged to the two of us, the ocean, and easy conversation that did not ask either of us to perform for anyone.

authored_arc_index.title: Do Not Make Me Guess
authored_arc_index.closing_anchor: The ocean did not promise anything. The future remained uncertain. But Greg was beside me, asking instead of assuming, making room instead of taking it. For that evening, it was enough.

authored_arc_index.title: The Ocean Remembers
authored_arc_index.closing_anchor: “I’ll try to answer.” I stayed until the lemonade was gone and the night air turned cold. Then Greg wrapped his jacket around my shoulders and walked me home, his hand holding mine all the way.

authored_arc_index.title: Jam Session
authored_arc_index.closing_anchor: “I do.” I kissed him under the community center awning while the last of the musicians carried instruments past me. The kiss was not a performance. It was simply another note in the conversation.

authored_arc_index.title: A Bad Day in G Major
authored_arc_index.closing_anchor: “They are not enough.” I smiled. The day was not perfect, but it had a map now.

authored_arc_index.title: Under the Same Stars
authored_arc_index.closing_anchor: For once, the future did not feel like an alarm. It felt like a road with somewhere to go.

authored_arc_index.title: Morning After Moonlight
authored_arc_index.closing_anchor: I had not planned to meet his son when I arrived with my suitcase. I had not planned to fall in love with a man who carried a guitar like a second heartbeat. The best parts of my life had begun without plans.

authored_arc_index.title: The Shape of Home
authored_arc_index.closing_anchor: But I placed the photograph on my own shelf beside the empty space where the tea belonged, and the room answered with a quiet sense of recognition. Home, I was learning, did not have to be a single address. It could be a pattern of places where my body stopped preparing to leave.

authored_arc_index.title: A Little Jealousy
authored_arc_index.closing_anchor: “Only in the best ways.” At home, he put on the record I liked and pulled me into the kitchen. I danced badly on purpose until I was laughing again.

authored_arc_index.title: The Long Way Back
authored_arc_index.closing_anchor: We ate it together. Slowly.

authored_arc_index.title: The Old Song
authored_arc_index.closing_anchor: The ocean kept time. Greg's fingers found mine, and the unfinished melody waited patiently beside me. I listened.

authored_arc_index.title: When the Van Breaks Down
authored_arc_index.closing_anchor: The calendar was enough. I kept the appointment.

authored_arc_index.title: The Almost Goodbye
authored_arc_index.closing_anchor: I both listened. The map stayed.

authored_arc_index.title: No More Running
authored_arc_index.closing_anchor: That was sufficient. The plan could wait.

authored_arc_index.title: The Door Left Open
authored_arc_index.closing_anchor: I slept easily that night. The room held us both.

authored_arc_index.title: Everything I Need to Say
authored_arc_index.closing_anchor: The melody would be warm. And it would be mine.

authored_arc_index.title: The House We Do Not Name
authored_arc_index.closing_anchor: Greg brought water while we sat together under the blanket. I told him the blanket was responding to character development, and the joke landed softly. So did the silence. We had crossed another threshold. The world had not changed shape, but the relationship had. At the end of the day, the next thing became clear: I put my toothbrush beside his and listened to the house learn the shape of two people. Greg's shoulder pressed against mine as the light moved across the room. The future arrived as a thing we could touch: a key, a song, a repaired hinge, a cup left on the counter for the person who would wake later. I let myself believe in the next morning without demanding that it guarantee every morning after. For now, that was enough.
